facts.statement: Stenomyti is an extinct genus of small aetosaurs.
facts.quote: Stenomyti is an extinct genus of small aetosaur.

facts.statement: The osteoderms of Stenomyti are nearly identical to those of Aetosaurus, suggesting that armor plates are not always reliable for distinguishing aetosaur species.
facts.quote: however its osteoderms are nearly identical to those of Aetosaurus which suggests that osteoderms are not always reliable taxonomic indicators for aetosaurs.

facts.statement: Fossils of Stenomyti huangae, including a skull and postcranial skeleton, were found in the Late Triassic Chinle Formation in the Eagle Basin of Colorado, United States.
facts.quote: which is known from a skull, postcranial skeleton and other referred material from the Late Triassic Chinle Formation, Eagle Basin of Colorado, United States.

facts.statement: Stenomyti belongs to the subfamily Aetosaurinae.
Stenomyti is classified within the family Stagonolepididae.
Stenomyti lived during the Norian to Rhaetian stages of the Late Triassic, from 227.3 to 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Rhaetian (227.3 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Stenomyti is closely related to Aetosaurus and lies outside the clades containing Typothoracisinae and Desmatosuchinae based on osteoderm and cranial similarities.
facts.quote: Based on its osteoderms, and other shared cranial characters with Aetosaurus, it was suggested that these taxa are closely related and lie outside the clade containing Typothoracisinae and Desmatosuchinae.
